title: Contextual Bandit Routing for Adaptive Multi-Agent Workflows
research_question: Can contextual bandit-based routing of decomposition, verifier, and escalation decisions reduce cost while preserving or improving task success in multi-agent workflows compared with static orchestration policies?
hypothesis: Because prior rejected ideas indicate that simple verifier allocation or risk escalation alone may lack novelty, a unified contextual bandit controller that adaptively routes among decomposition depth, verifier usage, and escalation actions using online feedback will outperform fixed workflow policies in both cost-efficiency and end-task quality.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated interest in uncertainty-aware adaptation, but also records rejected workflow ideas focused narrowly on verifier allocation or escalation. This suggests a gap: workflow optimization methods for agent systems may need a broader adaptive decision layer rather than a single control knob. Borrowing the feedback-loop view from self-adaptive systems, an online contextual bandit can decide when to decompose further, invoke a verifier, or escalate, turning orchestration into a learnable control problem with clearer novelty and measurable outcomes.
